annotation.reasoning_summary: The dataset represents specific real-world housing blocks managed by housing associations. Despite the numeric attributes regarding counts and percentages, these are features of the housing objects themselves rather than an area-wide statistical lattice or a thematic coverage classification. The polygon topology suggests isolated regions rather than a full administrative partition.
The layer maps distinct archaeological findings and locations (beerputten/finds) as points, which are identifiable real-world objects/assets.

The dataset maps specific archaeological find locations as points. Each point represents a distinct, real-world archaeological find or object associated with a specific site, making it a clear case of ObjectDS.

The polygons represent specific areas in parks with barbecue restrictions. Since they are isolated patches rather than an exhaustive tiling of the city or reporting units, they are classified as PlainVectorRegion and PatchDS.

The layer represents specific, named conservation areas (protected stads- en dorpsgezichten). These are treated as distinct bounded objects or sites rather than reporting units or an exhaustive full-area coverage. The low shared boundary ratio and low convex hull fill ratio confirm these are discrete features, not a tessellation.
